The very fact that according to the earlier text Rule 98 bis this Trial Chamber and this Tribunal was able to make judgements of acquittal and that now we have the undivided opinion that according to the text of the Rule 98 bis now that is in force it is almost impossible to enter a judgement of acquittal which underlines the difference between the two texts and without a doubt the former text of Rule 98 bis was more favourable for the accused. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, very briefly. First off, just again so the record is clear, I didn't say there were no differences in the Rule. I said that the legal standard had not changed and that the other aspects in our view were procedural changes and did not substantively -- substantially prejudice the rights of the accused. I did not say and do not say now that there were no changes. Secondly, and just as a point of information, and I'm just simply raising the issue, Your Honour. I don't know, as I stand here, I don't know the answer. I'm not sure whether anybody in the courtroom knows the answer. I'm not sure that it is correct to say that under the old Rule a part of a count could be a unit of acquittal. I don't know that that's the case. And the Chamber might want to research that and inquire into that before making a ruling. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber would like to withdraw. We shall take 20 minutes, perhaps less, and make a ruling when we get back. --- Break taken at 4.40 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will hand down its oral decision. I shall read it out slowly so that the interpreters can translate it properly. Oral decision pertaining to the request presented by the Petkovic Defence. The Petkovic Defence counsel today principally and as a preliminary submitted to the Trial Chamber the question of the interpretation and application of Rule 98 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. It holds that this Rule in its version dated the 8th of December, 2004, cannot be applied in this particular case because Rule 6(D) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence provides that, and let me read it out: "An amendment shall enter into force seven days after the date of issue of an official Tribunal document containing the amendment but shall not operate to prejudice the rights of the accused in any pending case." The Prosecution responds by saying that this is a procedural rule that can be instantly applied, which therefore does not substantially prejudice the accused. The Trial Chamber notes that this Rule, this amended 98 bis Rule has already been applied on several occasions in other cases which were pending at the time this Article was adopted. The Trial Chamber, in addition, feels that this Rule, i.e., a procedural Rule, can be instantly applied unless it prejudices the accused. The Trial Chamber is not convinced that an irremediable prejudice is -- let me read it again. The Trial Chamber is not convinced that the accused have suffered an irremediable prejudice. In this case the accused may argue that there is no element pertaining to the counts, and in addition, the accused at the time the judgement is handed down can be acquitted. The Defence counsel, moreover, submits that Rule 72 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence did not entitle them to attack the indictment because of the date on which this Rule was adopted and because of the date of the amended indictment. The Prosecution responded by saying that the Defence teams had had the possibility to file preliminary motions which it didn't do on this particular matter. The Trial Chamber notes that the indictment could have been the subject of a preliminary motion after the 15th of December, 2004. The Trial Chamber would like to say that if the Defence teams had felt that the amendment of Rule 98 bis could have adverse effects as far as human rights are concerned, a fair trial, expeditious trial, and the presumption of innocence, in that case it should have seized the Trial Chamber as soon as possible and should not have waited for the 98 bis procedure to be applied. Consequently, the requests filed by the Petkovic Defence team are dismissed. The Trial Chamber would therefore like to ask the Petkovic Defence team to address paragraphs 229 and following of the indictment on those counts. We have now handed down our decision, and I will give the floor back to the Petkovic Defence team so that it resumes its 98 bis submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm absorbing it as we go along, I'm trying to see whether Your Honours are making it expressly clear that the view which has been expressed in the course of today's submissions that the current Rule 98 bis does not permit us to do anything other than attack entire counts in the indictment, and that -- I'd rather understand that's the thrust of Your Honour's specific mention of paragraphs 229 and following of the indictment. Do I understand that correctly, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I want to be crystal clear about that. In that case -- well, I have no submissions then on the part of the application which Ms. Alaburic indicated was going to fall to me. I obviously invite my learned leader just to indicate then to Your Honours whether we, the team, have further submissions to make.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, right at the beginning we would like to seek leave to appeal against the decision on the interpretation and application of Rule 98 bis. Secondly, in accordance with your decision on our motion to strike some modes of criminal responsibility that are not within the jurisdiction of this Tribunal, I would like to remind you of that motion, and in accordance with the decision of the Trial Chamber I would like you to rule on this motion. This motion filed by General Petkovic's Defence is as follows: We would like to remind Your Honours to a pending motion filed by the Petkovic Defence in February 2007. It was sought that the Prosecution be ordered to strike some parts of the paragraphs 218, 224, 225, and 226 of the indictment where all the accused are charged with the following four modes of criminal responsibility: Co-perpetration; indirect co-perpetration; three, indirect perpetration of all the crimes that are alleged in the indictment; and, four, aiding and abetting of the joint criminal enterprise. In its motion, the Prosecution claimed, and it claims today, that in 2006 the jurisprudence of this Tribunal has established beyond any doubt that those forms of criminal responsibility are not under the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Tribunal, and those forms of criminal responsibility are not recognised either by the Statute or by the international case law. This was explicitly confirmed in the judgements and decisions by various Trial and Appeals Chambers in the cases Stakic, Milutinovic, Cermak and Markac, Popovic et al. On the 25th of April, 2007, this Trial Chamber ruled on this motion filed by the Petkovic Defence stating that to make a decision on this motion at that stage of the proceedings could disrupt the proceedings and unnecessarily tax the resources of the parties and that the decision would be made at an appropriate time when the Trial Chamber would rule on 98 bis motions before the beginning of the Defence case. In other words, the Trial Chamber postponed ruling on the Petkovic Defence motion until such time when decisions are made on the 98 bis motions. The Defence, let me remind you, was not allowed to appeal against this decision, but the Defence did file an appeal ex lege pursuant to Rule 72; it was rejected and a decision, the explanation, was that the decision of the Trial Chamber to rule on the merits of the case -- the merits of the motion filed by the Petkovic Defence before the beginning of the case would not be prejudicial to the accused and that a decision of the Appeals Chamber on the merits of the case would be ultra vires. So I conclude that in opposition to what the Trial Chamber ruled on the 24th of April, 2007, the Defence now expects the Trial Chamber to rule on the motion dated the 12th of February, 2007, motion to strike portions of paragraphs 218, 224, 225, 226, in relation to those forms -- four forms of criminal responsibility. The Defence believes that it would be unnecessary to present any further documents in this regard, because all the arguments have been made explicit in the motion filed by the Petkovic Defence. The Prosecution has had an opportunity to reply to those motions, and has indeed done so. Let me just note that this indictment is the only indictment that is valid before this Tribunal. This is the indictment under which the accused are tried. This is the only indictment that contains those controversial forms of criminal responsibility. We believe that this is extremely important, because these modes of criminal responsibility are not ascribed to the accused for just some of the offences listed in the indictment but for all of the offences that are alleged there. It would be extremely unfair and contrary to Articles 20 and 21 of the Statute for the Defence case to begin before this issue has been dealt with and ruled on. The motion to strike some modes of criminal responsibility from the indictment in its motion the General Petkovic Defence invites the Trial Chamber, in accordance with Rule 54 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, to consider the -- whether it is possible for some of the portions of the indictment to remain, and we will move that some parts of some of the counts of the indictment be stricken from the indictment which in our belief, based on the best standards of proof applied in Article -- in Rule 98 bis, can lead us to conclude that the Prosecution has failed to prove that the accused have committed those crimes. And now I would like to invite my colleague Mr. Nicholas Stewart to present his opinion to the -- or his views to the Trial Chamber under Article 54 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Two requests. There's a request for certification of appeal and another request pertaining to the modes of responsibility which was the subject of several written submissions. The Appeals Chamber had ruled that the Trial Chamber would rule on this when addressing Rule 98 bis. If I have understood you correctly, Mr. Stewart is going to take the floor and address this particular issue. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We believe that Rule 54 makes it possible, regardless of the existence and interpretation of Rule 98 bis, to initiate an argument on the viability of those counts in the indictment in light of the question whether the Prosecution has managed to prove those counts or not, because we believe that Rule 54 allows the Trial Chamber to intervene in the text of the indictment regardless of Rule 98 bis. So we thought that we would be making submissions under Rule 98 bis now. We would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the decision I handed down a few minutes ago you understood that we have been seized of Rule 98 bis. We have not been seized of the indictment. I would like this to be very clear in your mind. Now, if you wish to address legal issues that pertain to the counts in the indictment you may, but that will be part of 98 bis and not of Rule 54. So don't try to come back through the back door, because the Trial Chamber has clearly indicated that it's only Rule 98 bis which we have currently been seized of. So if Mr. Stewart would like to take the floor and discuss forms of responsibility, because the Trial Chamber, when it hands down its oral decision in two weeks' time, will have to state what it holds true, you can then of course add to your submissions, but you don't have to. It's for you to see what you wish to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I believe -- no, Your Honour. I think it is futile to provide any further explanations regarding the four forms of criminal responsibility that we propose be stricken from the indictment, because this has been explained in great detail in our motions. What we asked regarding Mr. Nicholas Stewart's submissions is leave to address you on the issue of the viability of some counts of the indictment, but that will be under Article 54. If this Trial Chamber considers that it is impossible to apply Rule 54 and that only Rule 98 bis can be applied as it -- as it has been interpreted in the jurisprudence, we will not be making any submissions, but we would like to ask you in that case to be allowed to file an appeal against this second decision, too, regarding this second motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will deliberate on your two certifications to appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, as far as the two requests for certification are concerned, the first request pertains to the oral decision which we have handed down. The Trial Chamber will not certify the appeal. As far as the decision relating to the fact that in addition to Rule 98 bis Rule 54 may be invoked, the Trial Chamber has been very clear on this matter and rejects certification to appeal also in this case. However, as far as the forms of criminal responsibility are concerned, the Trial Chamber will wait to see what the Prosecution will say, and the Trial Chamber, when it hands down its oral decision, will respond on the matter, but we will only respond when we will know what the Prosecution has to say about it. This is what we wish to state. Mrs. Alaburic, if you'd like to take the floor again, you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in view of the fact that in conformity with your ruling we find that based on Rule 98 bis we are really dealing with just mere formality and that we are not allowed to prove anything unless we have valid evidence regarding the entirety of the indictment, then according to the Rule interpreted in that way we cannot enter a request for judgement of acquittal and the four challenged types of responsibility because the Trial Chamber has ruled that they are outside the jurisdiction of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The Prosecution, interpreter's correction, not the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Alaburic, we didn't say that. We said that as far as criminal responsibility is concerned, the Trial Chamber will respond when it hands down its decision orally since this issue was raised on the 12th of February, 2007. The Appeals Chamber had then clearly stated that the Trial Chamber should rule on the matter when the -- as part of 98 bis. So we will rule on the matter as part of 98 bis. This is what the Appeals Chamber had asked us to do. This is what I wanted to tell you. But we will only take our decision once we have heard what the Prosecution has to say. For the time being, we don't know. If you have anything to add on the counts, you have the floor. No?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I would just like to repeat what I said earlier. There seems to be a misunderstanding. As for the charges in the indictment, if Rule 98 bis is interpreted in such a way as we can succeed with a certification only if there is evidence which relates to all the incidents in one of the counts, I have to say that for each of the counts of the indictment there is at least one piece of evidence so that we cannot submit the submission -- a valid submission which relates to every count in the indictment. With respect to the reaction of the accused, I would like to remind you that when we say that there is evidence and proof for each count in the indictment, that does not mean for each of the incidents in the counts in the indictment. It doesn't mean proof and evidence for each of the accused, and we [indiscernible] dealing with evidence for which I say has -- is credible and has probative value, but it is a fact that there is just one witness or perhaps one piece of documentary evidence with -- relating to each of the counts regardless of the probative value of each of those pieces of evidence which is the legal standard for the application of Rule 98 bis. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I just raise one more point. This is a genuine teamwork. You can see we're popping up and down in turn. So far as what Your Honour's said about the modes of criminal responsibility and the -- the February motion is concerned, the Prosecution did respond to that in the formal full way. We put in our written motion. They put in a written response. We have made no further submissions at all today on the substance of that matter. With respect, we don't really follow why the Prosecution then needs or indeed has any right to respond. There are two ways of doing it we suggest. Either we stand on the submissions we've made and the Prosecution stand on the submissions they've made, or - and we're in Your Honours' hands on this - if there is to be further submission by the Prosecution, further argument by the Prosecution, then in fairness in these particular circumstances we should then have the opportunity of replying to those submissions. It's -- it's both or neither we suggest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite right. Yes, you're quite right. So in the minds of the Judges of the Bench, there is no ambiguity. When the Prosecution will have the floor as part of the time allocated to it, either it will say, "I refer to my written submissions as regards that particular matter," and the Prosecution will say no more and the Trial Chamber will then hand down its oral decision after having scrutinised your written submissions and their written submissions, of course. But if Mr. Scott orally adds further elements, then of course you will have the floor and you may respond. That will not be an issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's most clear and most helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we still have one hour, and since time is of the essence, I shall now give the floor to the Defence of Coric or Pusic, unless they prefer to take the floor tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. That's precisely what I wanted to propose to the Trial Chamber. Since I have less than an hour left now and this would break up my presentation if I were to go ahead today, it would mean a great deal if I could start tomorrow and complete it tomorrow, and I don't think we'd lose any time that way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Now, when the question of time was raised, since we still have the Coric Defence and the Pusic Defence, we have already said that we won't be using a whole session. Now, it depends how long the Prosecution is going to take. The time set was nine hours earlier on, so as the time has been reduced, we're interested in how much time the Prosecution will need for its response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Prosecution for the moment is not in a position to say that. It has to wait to hear what Defence counsel of Coric have to say and yourself, and starting from there we'll see, but it's clear that they are not going to use up -- am I mistaken, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think where we are at the moment, Your Honour, I don't expect that the Prosecution will use anything like nine hours. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, the simplest way to proceed is we'll see you tomorrow. We have a hearing tomorrow afternoon. Therefore, we will meet at a quarter past 2.00 tomorrow, which should enable the Coric Defence to have its complete speech without having to divide it between today and tomorrow. So I wish you a pleasant evening, and we will all meet again tomorrow afternoon. Thank you very much. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of January, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 25
